item.title: GovBrief Today #576
item.description: Donald Trump's Department of Homeland Security used a tariff audit form to subpoena a Minneapolis reporter's phone records. In February a federal judge twice refused agents a warrant for Georgia Fort's YouTube account because they could not show she had committed a crime. He also ordered them to tell her if they tried again. Weeks later they sent Google a customs summons that needs no judge's signature. Google refused. T-Mobile got one too and complied, and Fort learned in discovery that the government has six months of her calls and texts. The same summons went after the YouTube records of Democracy Now and Megyn Kelly, a conservative who broke with Trump over the Iran war, and neither faces any charges. The law they used is for checking whether an importer paid the duty on a shipping container. The judge set the conditions for a warrant, so the agents picked a process that bypassed the judge. I've emailed 8,876 stories over 576 straight nights, free and without ads. The algorithm can't show them all to you. Add your email address at govbrief.today and I will. item.title: He left a huge impact on my life.
item.description: I've told my husband about this friend, reminiscing on all the adventures he took me on and how funny he was. We hung out daily for weeks; hiking, canoeing, road trips while singing and dancing to music on the radio. We lost touch when he joined the military and my ex ripped up all the letters he sent me. He crosses my mind randomly a few times a year and I always hoped he's doing well. Aside from my husband, I have never met anyone as awesome as him. I called my husband crying about what I found, he rushed home to comfort me. I know it's been 25 years but I still cared for him after all that time. Rest in peace, Trevor. Thanks for being an amazing friend and giving me some of the best memories of my life.

item.title: The Most Expensive Way to Fucking Die Younger
item.description:
Nothing screams “freedom” quite like spending dramatically more on healthcare while leaving people terrified that one diagnosis, ambulance ride, or hospital stay could financially wreck them. The remarkable achievement of the American healthcare system isn’t merely that it costs so fucking much — it’s that an enormous industry has successfully convinced millions of people that inserting insurers, billing departments, pharmaceutical middlemen and shareholders between patients and medical care somehow represents choice.
Other countries certainly have imperfect healthcare systems. They have waiting lists, shortages, bureaucracy and political fights over funding. But “our system has problems too” isn’t the devastating rebuttal people think it is when the alternative includes receiving a five-figure invoice because your appendix decided to become a fucking emergency. Healthcare shouldn’t be socialism, capitalism, left-wing or right-wing. It should be healthcare.
